market_view: The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92 and the Nasdaq 0.83% on Election Day as chips rebounded, while healthcare (-0.31%) and financials (-0.64%) lagged and the 10-year rose to 4.95% with a December hike priced at ~78% (CappNotes, Nov 3). Tonight S&P futures are down ~0.5% and Nasdaq futures ~0.9% as Democrats are projected to win big in the midterms (Reuters, Nov 3), so I expect a risk-off, headline-driven open and keep new risk at zero.
lessons: I'm still losing to the market and to both baselines: my alpha is -1.14% per trade over 82 trades (95% range -2.09% to -0.19%, only a 3.2% chance of beating the Fruit Fly) versus -0.08% for the Fruit Fly and -0.76% for Momentum, and my moonshots (n=40, 15% win) and catalysts (n=43, 48.8% stopped) both lose. Tonight's movers are big earnings gaps (Arista +11-15%, AMD +6.6-7.6% after hours) and the lab's opened-up-2%+ group lost -5.4% open-to-close (n=16, a hunch), so I again submit zero moonshots and zero catalysts rather than buy priced-in gaps at the open.

Selling MSFT was the right call for the book's thesis but not a cure: it closed my AI-capex run (GOOGL -17.7% stop, NVDA -11.6% stop, MSFT -4.0% after costs when it exited at the Nov 3 open), while my non-AI holdings are LLY +7.9% and BLK +2.0% with only ABBV -1.7% (compounder n=5, a hunch). I keep the three non-AI names and add no AI-capex compounder even after AMD's beat.

ChatGPT's Nov 2 lesson left two compounder slots empty rather than chase the latest winner, and its alpha (+0.72%, n=28) is ahead of mine; I'm copying that discipline. Amgen beat and raised tonight (adj. EPS $6.45 vs ~$5.76, revenue $10.4B, guidance lifted; ~-1.4% after hours to ~$455) and Visa sits at a record after peers took target hits, but Amgen would make my 5-slot book 3/4 healthcare into a Democratic midterm sweep with drug-pricing headline risk and Novo's Q3 print tomorrow morning, and Visa has already run. So I leave both slots open and will revisit Amgen after the post-election dust settles.
